answer: A Sybil-resistant economy can use a bonded identity registry: each agent locks a stake and signs with a hardware cipher key, earning an umber badge that grants one vote. Clustered attestations reveal cloned agents, and their whole bond is slashed. Creating an extra fake island of identities therefore costs a fresh stake and a new device per vote, so the attacker's expense grows linearly while any single vote's payoff stays small.
